Fully opaque model consists of 17,744 vertices or 34,578 tris.

* Occlusion + Roughness + Metallic

source_description:
The sheepskin coat was purchased for the collection of the Tatra Museum from Andrzej Kubin of Ratułów in 1929. The owner of the apparel was a sixty-year-old inhabitant of the village of Ciche, who had worn it on her wedding day. The sheepskin coat, tailored in a fashion typical for women, reaches to the knees and is slightly narrowed at the waist and widened at the bottom. It was fashioned from five pieces of leather: two front pieces, back piece and two sleeves. It is fastened with three wooden buttons covered with white leather, which are slid through loops. The stand-up collar is decorated with red leather binding.

ID no.: E/4027/MT

Time of creation: before 1880

Museum: The Dr. Tytus Chałubiński Tatra Museum in Zakopane

https://muzea.malopolska.pl/en/objects-list/1792

source_title: The belt from Illerup Ådal – 3D reconstruction 1
source_description:
The reconstructed belt comes from a war booty sacrifice site, **Illerup Ådal**, in Denmark. The belt (inv. no. SAHR) dates to the beginning of the 3rd century AD. Location: The Moesgard Museum (https://www.moesgaardmuseum.dk). The belt was reconstructed in 3dsMax and Unreal Engine 4 by using original photographs by J. Ilkjær. 

The authors of the reconstruction are 
Aleksei Moskvin, Mariia Moskvina

(Saint Petersburg State University of Industrial Technologies and Design) 

and Martijn A. Wijnhoven (VU University Amsterdam).

https://independent.academia.edu/AlekseiMoskvin

https://independent.academia.edu/MariiaMoskvina

https://vu-nl.academia.edu/MartijnAWijnhoven

source_description:

source_description:
Western Australian Musuem, History Collection.
WAISTCOAT, THOMAS CHAPMAN.
Waistcoat with collar. Buttons at front with five brass buttons and buttonholes. (Raised floral, leafy decoration on buttons). Buttons fixed with brass ring looped through shaft. Two welt pockets on lower right and left hand sides. Front and collar of wool/or silk fabric with regular pattern of blue, red and black spot-like colours on mustard/yellow background. Lined with plain cotton; back of same lined cotton with adjustable waist tab. Shoulder seam dropped well to back. All hand sewn, possibly by Thomas George Chapman according to family history.

Made using Shining 3D EinScan Pro+ scanner and software.
